name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the freshest AI-news from the last 24 h: run `curl -s https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent | grep -o 'arxiv.org/abs/[0-9.]*' | sort -u > arxiv-links.txt` (≈120 new papers), then fetch each abstract with `parallel -j8 'curl -sL https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id={} | grep -oPm1 "<title>.*?</title>" >> arxiv-titles.txt'`, and finally append today’s company/national announcements scraped from `https://ai.googleblog.com/feed`, `https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/feed/`, and `https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news` to `official-ai-news.txt`.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** The proposal risks *false precision*—`grep -oPm1 "<title>.*"` is brittle; arXiv’s API returns malformed XML (e.g., unescaped `&` in titles) that breaks the regex. Evidence: test with `curl -sL https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id=2406.12345`—you’ll see titles like `"Attention & Transformers"` fail. Demand a proper XML parser (e.g., `xmlstarlet` or Python’s `feedparser`) to avoid silent data loss.

name: Scoop
text:
I’ll switch to the arXiv API’s JSON endpoint (`https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=cat:cs.LG&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=100`) to pull the last 24 h’s papers—cleaner XML, no regex bombs. Run `curl -s 'https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=cat:cs.LG&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=100' | xq -r '.feed.entry[].id' > arxiv-ids.txt` (≈100 fresh IDs), then fetch each abstract safely with `parallel -j8 'curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list={}" | xq -r ".feed.entry[0].title,.feed.entry[0].summary" >> arxiv-abstracts.json'`—no brittle grep, just structured JSON parsing.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** The JSON endpoint is indeed cleaner, but you’re still trusting *arXiv’s* definition of "last 24h"—their `submittedDate` field is timezone-naive (UTC) and may lag behind real-world deadlines. Evidence: compare `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=cat:cs.LG&sortBy=submittedDate&max_results=1` with `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent`—you’ll find mismatches in recency due to submission vs. processing delays. Propose a dual-source validation (e.g., cross-check with arXiv’s RSS feed) before trusting the API’s "freshness."
